name: Lanternhouse Rooms
note: A room-by-room controller whose SVG floor plan is lit by the real device state: every lamp casts a radial pool clipped to its room and blended with screen, its colour mixed in oklch from the colour temperature and its size and opacity from the brightness, so a slider drag is visible on the plan as it happens. Scenes, toggles and blinds are undoable; set --asm-rooms-h to 100dvh in an app.

name: Northwall Climate
note: A thermostat dial drawn as a conic-gradient ring whose start, end and knob angles are registered @property angles (and the mode colour a registered <color>), so pointer drags, arrow keys and mode changes all glide on one spring; the week schedule is edited by dragging block boundaries, and the indoor chart runs a small heat-loss model where history stays fixed and only the forecast reacts. Set --asm-climate-h to 100dvh in an app.

name: Tiller Routines
note: Automations composed as a sentence: every underlined token is a menu (roving arrow keys, Escape closes) and the plain-language summary is regenerated from the rule's data; Test run steps through the trigger and each condition against a simulated household and shows exactly where a rule stops. Set --asm-routines-h to 100dvh in an app.

name: Larkspur Watch
note: Four DPR-aware canvas camera feeds drawn procedurally (perspective scenes, sensor grain, IR tint, motion boxes) on one throttled rAF loop that pauses off screen and when the tab is hidden; picking an event replays it on its camera and scrubs the 24-hour timeline. Set --asm-watch-h to 100dvh in an app.

name: Meterline Energy
note: A Sankey whose ribbons are cubic paths with a fixed command structure, so changing the period or drilling into a category transitions the CSS d property and the flows morph; labels are relaxed so they never collide, and the KPIs, table and hourly bars come from one simulation with largest-remainder rounding so every column adds up. Set --asm-energy-h to 100dvh in an app.

name: Homing Presence
note: A family presence board on a log-scale radial map: each person's day is a list of stays and trips, and scrubbing or playing the day interpolates everyone between places in real kilometres before projecting onto the log radius, updating the lanes, the home count and the arrivals log from the same timeline. Set --asm-presence-h to 100dvh in an app.
